item.title: AI Gains Spread Amid Global Economic Fragmentation
item.description:
AI Gains Spread Amid Global Economic Fragmentation

New research shows that AI breakthroughs remain clustered in a few economies, yet the productivity gains can diffuse worldwide; the extent of that diffusion depends on how fragmented the global economy has become.

🔍 Overview

  • Artificial intelligence is advancing at the same time as the global economy is becoming more fragmented.
  • AI innovation is concentrated in a small number of economies, while the gains from AI depend on technologies, intermediate inputs, data, investment, and know‑how moving across borders.
  • Fragmentation can therefore shape not only the size of the global gains from AI, but also who receives them.

🧩 Layers of the AI ecosystem

Layer Typical participants Geographic concentration
Frontier innovators Entities that create frontier AI models Highly concentrated, especially in the US, China, and the EU
Supply‑chain and infrastructure providers Producers of semiconductors, cloud services, AI‑enabled machinery, etc. Much broader
Adopters Firms that use AI‑related hardware, software, services, or AI‑enabled intermediate inputs Much broader

⚙️ Diffusion channel and model results

  • Firms can become more productive without developing AI themselves: they can use better semiconductors, software, cloud services, or AI‑enabled machinery produced elsewhere.
  • Our benchmark simulation using the IMF’s ECLIPSSE model illustrates the size of this diffusion channel.
  • When AI raises productivity at the frontier and also improves the efficiency with which AI‑related intermediate inputs are used elsewhere, modeled global GDP is 1.64 % above the baseline.
  • The gains are 2.28 % in the US, 1.87 % in China, 1.93 % in the EU and 0.94 % in the rest of the world.
  • These numbers are scenario‑based model estimates, not forecasts. Their purpose is to show how gains propagate through production networks.

📉 Impact of economic fragmentation

  • Barriers to trade and technology diffusion – tariffs, export controls, investment screening, restrictions on data flows, and incompatible digital regulations – can make AI‑related inputs more costly or less accessible.
  • These channels are part of the broader costs of geoeconomic fragmentation documented by Aiyar et al. (2023).
  • Fragmentation can also slow innovation at the frontier itself by reducing collaboration, knowledge flows, market scale and access to complementary inputs.
  • In our simulations, trade fragmentation alone reduces global GDP gains from 1.64 % to 1.49 %; the rest‑of‑world gain slips from 0.94 % to 0.93 %.
  • When fragmentation also slows frontier AI progress, global gains fall further to 1.29 % and rest‑of‑world gains to 0.85 %.
  • It is that fragmentation damages the innovation process that creates technologies for everyone.

💡 Policy options for non‑frontier economies

  • For economies not at the technological frontier, preserving diversified links may be a valuable form of economic optionality.
  • The MENAP economies in our sample maintain significant trade and investment links with the US, Europe and China; that diversification can become an asset if geopolitical rivalry intensifies.
  • Simulations compare ‘choosing sides’ with three more active strategies:
    1. Connector strategy – lowering lawful trade and regulatory frictions with partners on multiple sides – can more than offset the losses from fragmentation in our experiment.
    2. Improving AI preparedness – upgrading digital infrastructure, skills, and institutions to raise the capacity to absorb AI.
    3. Strengthening local AI‑related capacity – developing domestic software, data, adaptation, and deployment services to deepen domestic gains.

#AI #globaltrade #economicfragmentation #productivity

Source: AI in a fragmenting world: Why ‘connector’ economies can still gain

item.title: Google launches AI‑powered voice assistant modes for Gmail, Docs, and Keep
item.description:
Google launches AI‑powered voice assistant modes for Gmail, Docs, and Keep

Google is rolling out AI‑powered voice assistant modes for Gmail, Docs, and Keep that let users manage the apps by talking to them.

🔍 Overview

Google’s new real‑time conversational features—Gmail Live, Docs Live, and Keep Live—extend the Gemini Live experience to its core productivity apps. The tools are designed to make it easier to note down or find specific information when you’re on the move or unable to interact manually.

🧩 How it works

  • The assistant listens to natural‑language voice commands and responds verbally while showing an on‑screen transcript.
  • Users can interrupt the conversation mid‑sentence or ask follow‑up questions without starting a new session.
  • If permission is granted, the assistant can pull data from Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web to personalize its output.

⚙️ Key details

Feature What it does
Gmail Live Surfaces details from your inbox without digging through threads; fetches information, summarizes it verbally, and links the source emails in the transcript.
Docs Live Formats ideas into structured documents based on conversational descriptions; can summarize longer documents or turn them into business proposals; can pull information from Gmail, Drive, Chat, and the web when allowed.
Keep Live Transcribes natural speech into notes; contextualizes entries without needing specific keywords; can add items like “ingredients for pesto” to a shopping list.

🚀 Availability

  • Previewed at Google I/O in May, the features are now rolling out globally in English on mobile platforms.
  • Gmail Live: Available on iOS and Android for users on Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra plans.
  • Docs Live: Coming to AI Pro and Ultra plans; available on both iOS and Android.
  • Keep Live: Coming to AI Pro and Ultra plans; Android only.
  • All three are “coming soon” for Workspace business customers.

💡 Why it matters

The voice‑first interface provides a hands‑free way to fetch information, summarize content, and transcribe notes, helping users stay productive when manual interaction isn’t practical.

#GoogleAI #VoiceAssistant #Productivity

Source: Google now lets you chat with Gmail, Docs, and Keep

item.title: Economic Impact and Productivity Gains from AI Adoption
item.description:
Economic Impact and Productivity Gains from AI Adoption

Recent analysis indicates that AI is driving significant shifts in labour productivity, with projections suggesting growth between 0.4-1.3 percentage points in high-exposure G7 countries and an estimated 0.2 percentage point boost in trend growth.

⚙️ Key details

  • Productivity improvements for many tasks are currently measured at approximately 50%.
  • Efficiency gains are observed in coding, translation, writing, and data analysis.
  • As agentic AI adoption grows, further increases in productivity are expected as entire functions become automated.
  • Historically, the benefits of such productivity improvements, like automation and machinery, have favored capital owners over labour.

💡 Why it matters

AI is acting as a tool for the democratisation of expertise and information, helping to offset skill and knowledge deficits.

  • Accessibility: The technology makes content more intuitive and easier to digest, bridging knowledge gaps.
  • Skill augmentation: Individuals with limited technical or mathematical skills can now produce sophisticated analytical models or perform complex tasks using natural language prompts.
  • Entrepreneurship: Barriers to starting a business are shifting from being capital-constrained to creativity-constrained, making one-man or resource-light companies more viable.
  • Competitive landscape: Smaller, leaner teams are increasingly able to compete with larger organizations.

🧩 User dynamics

User Category Expected Outcome
Average users Higher quantity/quality output and time savings on routine work
Superusers Dramatically scaled output
Misusers Accuracy and reliability issues

#AI #Productivity #Economics #Technology

Source: Will AI become the Great Equaliser?
